title: Infantry Squad Leader (Sgt) NMOS (0311, 0331, 0341, 0352), DC PP&O
raw_text:
16. MOS 0365, Infantry Squad Leader (Sgt) NMOS (0311, 0331, 0341, 0352), DC
PP&O

    a. Summary. THIS IS AN OBSOLETE MOS, NO LONGER IN USE IN THE TABLE OF
ORGANIZATION OF THE MARINE CORPS. THIS MOS IS MAINTAINED IN THE MOS MANUAL
BECAUSE IT APPEARS IN THE RECORDS OF MARINES STILL ON ACTIVE DUTY OR THE
RESERVES. Infantry Squad Leaders are created via the squad leader
development program (SLDP) by a lateral move from the infantry MOS of
Rifleman (0311), Machine Gunner (0331), Mortarman (0341), or Antitank Missile
Gunner (0352). SLDP was designed to synchronize the training and education
of a second term infantryman with the assignments process that results in a
more mature, better trained and educated squad leader. Volunteers gain
priority placement in advanced infantry training and the Sergeants Course
which professionalizes the squad leader billet and enhances the capabilities
of Marine infantry squad leaders for operations in complex and distributed
environments. The Infantry Squad Leader plans for assigned missions and
carries out the orders issued by the platoon commander. He/She is also
responsible for the discipline, training, control, conduct, and welfare of
his squad at all times, as well as the condition, care, and economical and



                                         3-36                        Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



effective use of its weapons and equipment. In combat, he is responsible for
the tactical employment, fire discipline, fire control, sustainment, and
maneuver of his squad during offensive, defensive, amphibious, and stability
operations. These leaders will be placed in squad billets based off original
MOS proficiency and strength.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) No courts martial convictions.

            (2) No adverse fitness reports within the last 12 months.

            (3) Must be a volunteer in the grade of corporal or sergeant.

            (4) No derogatory Page 11 entries within the last 12 months.

            (5) Must have a minimum of 3 and no more than 6 years in service.

        (6) Must be complete in all professional military education
requirements for corporal.

        (7) No non-judicial punishments (NJPs) within the last 12 months and
with no more than 2 NJPs during the current contract.

            (8) Must be a graduate of:

                (a) Advanced Mortar Course (M10H5H2 or M03H5H4).

                (b) Advanced Machinegun Course (M10H6A2 or M03H6A4).

                (c) Advanced Anti-Armor Course (M10MUR2 or M03MUR4).

                (d) Scout Sniper Course (M0281Z9 or M0381Z4 or M1081Z2).

                (e) Advanced Infantry Marine Course (M10M3X2 or M03M3X4).

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the Sergeants Course at one of the following locations:

                (a) (M02T4M5), Staff Noncommissioned Officers Academy, Quantico,
VA.

                (b) (M09T4M2), Staff Noncommissioned Officers Academy, 29 Palms,
CA.

                (c) (M21T4M1), Staff Noncommissioned Officers Academy, Kaneohe
Bay, HI.

                (d) (M03T4M5), Staff Noncommissioned Officers Academy, Camp,
Lejeune, NC.

            (e) (M22T4M1), Staff Noncommissioned Officers Academy, FPO AP
Okinawa, Japan.

            (f) (M10T4M6), Staff Noncommissioned Officers Academy, MCB Camp
Pendleton, CA.




                                         3-37                           Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (e), Infantry Training and Readiness Manual and Marine Corps
Warfighting Publication 11.2-Marine Rifle Squad.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.
common_text: In addition to the Infantry Officer, Marine Gunner, and Infantry Unit Leader, the 03 Infantry Occupational Field is comprised of the following specialties rifleman, light armor vehicle marine, reconnaissance marine, machine gunner, mortarman, and antitank missile gunner. Regardless of specialty, Infantry Marines are primarily employed in units from the team to regimental-level in order to locate, close with, and destroy the enemy in all environments and weather conditions, during both the day and night. Excluding Light Armored Reconnaissance Units, Infantry Marines are principally trained to operate light and fast on foot. Infantry units are capable of multiple methods of entry and insertion, embarking aboard and fighting from helicopters, assault amphibious vehicles, motorized tactical vehicles, ultra-light tactical vehicles, and small boats. As the principal component of a Marine Air-Ground Task Force's ground combat element, Infantry Marines must be able to operate effectively in austere and distributed environments characterized by friction, uncertainty, and chaos. All Infantry Marines must be physically dominant and masters of small arms marksmanship, tactical combat casualty care, and battle drills in every operating environment. Infantry units must be comprised of Marines proficient in the employment of demolitions, rockets, machineguns, mortars, and missile systems and capable of directing supporting arms. Infantry Marines must also be proficient in field craft and capable of employing unmanned systems, limited information warfare, and non-lethal systems.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
